attempts.summary: Built a 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster (MariaDB 10.6.28 + galera-4) from scratch on node1/node2/node3 (RHEL7, no server packages pre-installed). Configured wsrep replication, opened firewalld Galera ports, bootstrapped the cluster, and loaded an application dataset (appdata.orders, 3 rows). Took the entire cluster down cleanly (node2, node3, then node1 last to guarantee safe_to_bootstrap), confirmed full outage, then restored it: bootstrapped node1 from its preserved grastate (seqno 9, safe_to_bootstrap:1) and rejoined node2/node3, recovering with all 4 committed rows (including a write made immediately before the outage) present and wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced on every node. Then executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured per-node boot_id + cluster/data health baselines, restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time via `sudo reboot` (never more than one down simultaneously), confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and verified each node auto-rejoined the cluster (size 3, Synced) with all 4 rows intact before moving to the next node.
